summary: Reproduced the reported Kimi-K3 strict structural-tag failure with the pinned xgrammar 0.2.1, then bumped active package variants to xgrammar 0.2.2, whose real structural-tag compiler preserves the named integer property's schema while still accepting an unknown property governed by the schema-valued additionalProperties. Added a registered regression covering all three cases.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction through xgrammar.Grammar.from_structural_tag: the invalid named value {"data":{"data":""}} was accepted. Raw output: reports/j-86666c13bf91/raw/regression-before.txt

Passing-after regression through the real xgrammar 0.2.2 structural-tag compiler: valid named integer accepted, invalid named object rejected, and valid unknown additional object accepted. Raw output: reports/j-86666c13bf91/raw/regression-after.txt
Full Kimi-K3 structural-tag unit file: 36 passed. Raw output: reports/j-86666c13bf91/raw/kimik3-full.txt

tests.command: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-86666c13bf91/venv/bin/python tomllib parse of all five modified pyproject files
tests.what_was_measured: All active package manifests changed by the dependency bump remain valid TOML. Raw output: reports/j-86666c13bf91/raw/pyproject-parse.txt

On one AMD Instinct MI355X, a 96x64 by 64x80 float32 GPU matmul matched an independent CPU float64 reference within rtol=2e-5 and atol=2e-5 (max absolute error 5.085926261472196e-06). This checks ROCm environment integrity and is not evidence for the CPU-only grammar fix. Raw output: reports/j-86666c13bf91/raw/gpu-numerical.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: One visible AMD Instinct MI355X executed the recorded numerical matmul check with torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 and HIP 7.2.26015; grammar correctness itself was tested CPU-only.

remaining_limitations: No Kimi-K3 model weights or serving deployment were exercised; the deterministic issue reproduction and fix verification use SGLang's actual structural-tag builder and xgrammar compiler.

The fix consumes xgrammar's released prebuilt 0.2.2 native binding at /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-86666c13bf91/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/xgrammar/libxgrammar_bindings.so; no SGLang or FlyDSL native source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
The intentionally disabled/commented xgrammar entry in python/pyproject_xpu.toml remains unchanged.
